system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general Warranty cap; 20% is available only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6m** — no authority has been given to use the conditional 20% fallback. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | **AUD 25,000** de minimis; **AUD 250,000** deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000** de minimis; **AUD 50,000** tipping basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore buyer thresholds** — the seller’s proposal materially restricts recovery through both elevated thresholds and a deductible basket. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims must be notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24 months** for general Warranty Claims, without extending that regime to other claim categories; 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s written approval. | **Reject and require 24 months** — the 18-month fallback is unauthorised and the proposed all-Claims overlay could erode separate protections. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same cap and time limit as general warranties. | Separate regime with a **100% purchase-price cap**, at least **six years**, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. | **Reject outright** — ownership, capacity and title risk must not be compressed into the general Warranty regime. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**, with no express fraud carve-out. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert a comprehensive non-waivable carve-out** — the seller’s universal language could improperly shelter intentional wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; no deemed disclosure through the data room, public registers or prudent searches. | **Delete the general disclosures and require specific fair disclosure** — bulk-source disclosure improperly transfers the identification and assessment burden to the buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket exclusion; if any knowledge qualifier remains, confine it appropriately and use named seller knowledge persons subject to reasonable enquiry, never affecting title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject the actual, adviser and constructive-knowledge bar** — “discoverable” information should not excuse undisclosed breaches or override protected categories. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller gives reasonable endeavours; condition is treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, although no final consent or evidence that its conditions are satisfied is disclosed. | Before Completion, require an **effective Bluefen consent** and evidence that every associated condition has been satisfied. | **Make effective unconditional consent and condition satisfaction a Completion condition** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and reasonable endeavours or mere delivery leaves material contract risk. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; a security release is to follow Completion, with no final discharge presently supplied. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion; any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require repayment and effective releases through the Completion funds flow** — an unsecured promise of a later release leaves the acquired group exposed to continuing debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** Completion bonuses are said to be a seller matter but are not separately itemised; on-costs are undetermined. | A specific funds-flow line item or other clear seller funding for the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Expressly allocate and seller-fund the bonuses and on-costs** — omitting them from the funds flow risks the target or buyer bearing a Completion-triggered seller liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment; DD-010 records **AUD 180,000** open, but this is not independently verified and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is supplied. | Broader protection for all Ironquay-related IP ownership, transfer, payment and third-party exposure, while preserving the contractual SOW3 payment cure; do not assume the AUD 180,000 is conclusively payable or not payable. | **Broaden the indemnity and verify the payment/assignment position** — a payment-only indemnity may not cure defective title or cover the full consequences of failed IP transfer. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosed facts do not establish access, exact scope, notification duty, breach or loss. | Evidence preservation, including logs; prompt investigation; continuing updates; buyer oversight and appropriate protection for resulting liabilities, without assuming a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or amount. | **Require preservation, investigation and update covenants with tailored protection** — the present uncertainty calls for process and risk allocation, not an unsupported conclusion in either direction. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total **AUD 330,000** and are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, necessity, termination rights, accrual and ordinary-course status; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Reserve position pending diligence and contractual review** — the disclosure does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, accrued, terminable or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller proposes that limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated, and treats Tax/IP as settled under the general regime. | Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, with no hidden override by general limitations. | **Reject the omnibus limitation architecture and specify each regime expressly** — otherwise negotiated protections may be unintentionally capped, time-barred or subjected to thresholds. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 internal share register as evidence that the Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, valid issue, encumbrance-free title, authority and capacity, supported by appropriate searches and Completion deliverables. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive proof** — a supplied internal register identifies the seller’s asserted source but is not independent verification of good title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the proposed general regime. | Treat Tax and IP terms as **open**, separately negotiate their warranties, indemnities, caps, periods and exclusions, and assume neither unlimited liability nor an agreed resolution. | **Expressly reserve and negotiate both regimes** — the seller cannot deem unresolved Tax/IP allocation settled through an unacceptable general limitation package. |
=== END ADVICE ===
